threads.thread_goal: Align on current-state workflows and confirm scope for standardisation

messages.text: Hi everyone, thanks for joining this project. We're kicking off the standardisation of patient intake and admin workflows across our units. The goal is to reduce errors, improve coordination, and make sure we're compliant with all current legislation. I'd like to start by understanding how intake and admin tasks currently run in each of your units. Can you share a quick overview of your current process? We'll use this to map out A1 and start on T1. Looking forward to hearing from you all.

Thanks for the clear kickoff. From our unit, intake starts with the healthcare assistant greeting the patient and collecting basic demographics. Then it goes to me or another admin staff member to verify ID and enter it into the system. After that, the nurse reviews consent forms. The challenge is that each unit seems to have slightly different forms and different handoff points. I think we need to be really clear about which units we're including in the first wave—are we looking at all three main units or starting smaller?

Good point. Our unit has a similar flow but we've added an extra step where the healthcare assistant confirms insurance details before the admin handoff. It's meant to reduce back-and-forth, but I'm not sure if it's actually helping or just adding time. Also, we use different consent forms for older adults versus general patients. Should we be standardising across all patient types in the first wave, or focusing on one scenario first?

I see the same variation here. We have three intake scenarios: adult, older adult, and disability support cases. Each has slightly different consent requirements and documentation needs. From a compliance perspective, I'd recommend we map all three, but maybe we pilot with just one or two to keep it manageable. What does everyone think about scope?

I agree with mapping all three scenarios—that's important for compliance. For the first standardisation wave, I'd suggest we focus on the two main units and include all three patient types. That gives us good coverage without overloading the pilot. We can roll out to the third unit in phase two. Does that work for everyone? Also, for the detail level in A1, I think we need to document each step, who does it, what forms are used, and where the handoffs happen. Clear enough?

That sounds right. Two main units, all three patient types, and detailed step-by-step maps. I can start documenting our unit's workflows this week. Should we also capture the pain points and variations as we go, or do that in a second pass?

I'd say capture them as you go—it'll be fresher and more accurate. I can do the same for our unit. One thing I want to flag: we need to make sure we validate these maps with at least one healthcare assistant and one nurse from each unit, as per the definition of done for T1. Should we schedule those validation conversations now or after we have the first drafts?

Good catch. Let's get the first drafts done by end of week, then schedule validation chats for early next week. That way we have time to refine before we move to the SOP design. I'll coordinate the validation schedule. Does everyone have access to the shared workspace where we'll be storing A1 and all the working docs?

Yes, I have access. Just to clarify—when we're documenting the current workflows, should we also note any compliance gaps we spot? Or is that something the quality and compliance officer will review separately?

Good question. I'd say note any obvious gaps you see, but don't try to solve them yet. That's part of the SOP design phase. For now, just document what's actually happening and flag concerns. I'll review everything from a compliance angle once we have the maps.

Alright, that's clear. So to summarise where we've landed: we're mapping two main units, all three patient types, with detailed steps and handoffs. We'll capture pain points and variations as we go. Validation with clinical staff happens early next week. And we flag compliance concerns but don't solve them yet. Is that right?

Perfect summary. That's exactly where we are. I'll get the shared workspace updated with a template for the workflow maps and a validation checklist. Everyone should have that by end of day. Let's aim to have first drafts of A1 ready by Friday EOD, and we'll schedule the validation calls for Monday and Tuesday. Sound good?

threads.thread_goal: Review and finalise the draft standard intake SOP and forms

messages.text: Hi all, thanks for getting the workflow maps done and validated. Now we're moving to the next phase: designing the standard intake SOP and unified forms. I've drafted a first version of A2 and A3 based on the maps and the compliance requirements we discussed. The SOP covers registration, identification, consent, and basic information capture. The forms include templates for adult, older adult, and disability support cases. Please review and comment on the draft—I'm looking for feedback on whether the steps are clear, whether the roles and responsibilities make sense, and whether anything is missing from a compliance or practical standpoint. The docs are in the shared workspace. Let me know your thoughts by Wednesday so we can refine before the compliance review.

Thanks for getting this done quickly. I've read through A2 and I think the core steps are solid. One thing I noticed: the SOP says the healthcare assistant should verify ID, but in our unit, that's always been an admin task. Is this a change we're intentionally making, or should we keep it as admin responsibility?

Good catch. Looking at the maps we did, it varies by unit. In our unit, the healthcare assistant does a preliminary check and the admin staff does the formal verification. I think the SOP should reflect that two-step approach—it reduces errors and makes sure both roles are clear. What do you think, 35334?

That makes sense. I was trying to simplify, but if the two-step approach is what's working in practice and reduces errors, we should keep it. I'll update A2 to reflect that. Healthcare assistant does preliminary check, admin staff does formal verification. Clear roles, less rework. Good feedback.

I've also reviewed A3 and the form templates. They look comprehensive, but I want to flag something on the consent section. For older adults and disability support cases, we need to be extra careful about capacity assessment and whether a guardian or advocate needs to be involved. The current draft doesn't explicitly address that. Should we add a decision tree or a separate guidance note?

That's a really important point. Capacity assessment is critical for compliance. I think a decision tree would be clearer than just a note—it helps staff know exactly when to escalate or involve a guardian. Can we add that to A3 before we send it for compliance review?

Absolutely. I'll add a capacity assessment decision tree to the older adult and disability support form templates. That's exactly the kind of detail we need to get right before pilot. Anything else on A2 or A3 that needs attention?

I've looked at the forms too. One small thing—the language in some sections is a bit formal. For patients with lower literacy or non-native speakers, it might be hard to understand. Should we simplify some of the wording, or is that something we address in training?

That's a good point. I think we should simplify the forms themselves—they're the primary document patients see. Training can support, but the forms should be as clear as possible on their own. 35334, can you review the language and simplify where possible?

Good point. I'll do a language review and simplify the forms. Clearer language helps everyone—patients, staff, and compliance. I'll have the updated versions ready by Wednesday EOD. Then we can send them to the quality and compliance officer for formal review. Does that timeline work?

Yes, that works. Once we get the compliance sign-off, we should be ready to lock in A2 and A3 for the pilot. I assume we'll also need to brief the healthcare assistants and nurses on the rationale behind the changes—especially the capacity assessment piece and the two-step ID verification. Should that be part of the training materials we're developing next?

Exactly. That's part of T6 and the training deck we'll be building in the next thread. For now, let's focus on getting A2 and A3 solid and through compliance review. I'll send the updated versions to the quality and compliance officer by Thursday and aim for their feedback by Friday. Once we have that, we can confirm D3 and D4 and move forward with training design. Sound good?

Sounds good. Just to confirm: once we have compliance sign-off, we're locking in A2 and A3 as the authoritative versions for the pilot, right? No more changes unless something critical comes up during the pilot itself?

Correct. Once compliance signs off and we confirm D3 and D4, A2 and A3 are locked for the pilot. If we find issues during the pilot, we'll document them and make adjustments in the post-pilot refinement phase. That's T9. For now, we're committing to these versions. Let's get the compliance review done and reconvene Friday to confirm.

threads.thread_goal: Lock training approach, materials, and schedule for the pilot

messages.text: Great news—we've got compliance sign-off on A2 and A3. Now let's focus on training. I've drafted A4 (the quick-reference checklist for healthcare assistants) and A5 (the training deck and FAQ). I've also sketched out a proposed training calendar that fits around shift patterns. The checklist is one page, covers key safety and consent checks, and uses simple language. The training deck covers the rationale for the changes, walks through the new SOP step-by-step, and includes scenarios. The FAQ addresses the top 10 questions I anticipate. Please review and give feedback on the format, content, and whether the training schedule works for your units. I'm aiming to lock this in by Monday so we can start scheduling sessions.

I've reviewed A4 and it's really clear. The checklist format works well—it's easy to reference during intake. One question: should we also create a version for admin staff, or is the checklist just for healthcare assistants? I'm thinking admin staff might benefit from a similar one-pager that covers their specific steps.

Good idea. Let me add an admin staff version to A4. Same format, but focused on ID verification, form entry, and handoff steps. I'll have that ready by tomorrow. Anything else on the checklist or the training deck?

I've looked at A5 and the training deck is solid. The scenarios are helpful. One thing I'd suggest: can we add a scenario that covers what to do if a patient refuses to provide certain information or if there's a capacity concern? That's a real situation we face, and staff need to know how to handle it.
Absolutely. I'll add two scenarios: one for patient refusal and one for capacity concerns. That's exactly the kind of real-world situation staff need to be prepared for. I'll update A5 by tomorrow.

Good additions. On the training schedule—I see you've proposed two live sessions per week for two weeks, plus async materials. That's 4 live sessions total. Given our staffing constraints, can we confirm that we can cover shifts while people are in training? I want to make sure we're not leaving units understaffed.

That's a good question. In our unit, we can cover two sessions per week without impacting patient care, but not more than that. If we do one session per week for four weeks instead, we'd have more flexibility. Would that work for everyone?

One per week for four weeks works better for us too. It also gives staff time to absorb the material and ask questions. Plus, we can do the async materials in between sessions. I think that's a better approach than cramming it into two weeks.

Got it. I'll revise the training schedule to one session per week for four weeks. That gives us better coverage and more time for staff to absorb the material. I'll also make sure the async materials are ready to go between sessions. For attendance, I'm aiming for at least 80% of target staff in each unit. Does that seem realistic?

80% is realistic if we give people enough notice and make it clear it's mandatory. I'd suggest we send out the training calendar at least two weeks in advance so people can plan. Also, should we record the live sessions for people who can't make it, or just rely on the async materials?

Good point. I'll record the live sessions and make them available as part of the async materials. That way, if someone can't attend live, they can still watch and learn. I'll also include a Q&A option for people who watch the recording. That should help us hit the 80% target. Let me get all these updates done by tomorrow and we can confirm the final training approach and schedule by Monday.
Sounds good. Just to confirm the training format: one live session per week for four weeks, recorded for async access, plus written async materials and the quick-reference checklists. Is that right?

Exactly. That's D5. One live session per week for four weeks, recorded, plus written materials and checklists. We'll also collect feedback after each session and adjust if needed. Once we confirm this approach on Monday, we'll move to locking in the specific dates and times for D6. Does everyone agree with this format?

Yes, I'm good with that. One thing to add to the agenda for Monday: we should also confirm who's going to deliver the training. Is it going to be you, 35334, or should we split it across a couple of people?

Good question. I can deliver the first session, but I think it would be good to have someone from each unit co-deliver or at least be present to answer unit-specific questions. That way, staff see familiar faces and feel more comfortable asking questions. I'll coordinate with you all on Monday to figure out the best arrangement. For now, let's get the materials finalized and we'll sort out the delivery logistics on Monday.

threads.thread_goal: Coordinate the pilot run and daily issue handling

messages.text: Alright, we're ready to launch the pilot. Training is done, materials are locked in, and staff are prepared. The pilot will run for two weeks starting Monday, 15th of next month, in Unit A. We'll be tracking errors, delays, and staff feedback using A6. Daily check-ins will happen at 4 PM each day—just a quick async update on how things are going, any blockers, and any issues we need to address. The goal is to catch problems early and adjust on the fly if needed. 529990, you'll be the primary contact for Unit A during the pilot. I'll be monitoring overall and we'll have a weekly sync with the full team. Let's confirm the exact dates and expectations for T7.

Got it. So pilot runs Monday 15th through Friday 26th—two weeks. I'll do the daily 4 PM check-ins and flag any issues. I've already briefed the team in Unit A and they're ready. One thing I want to confirm: if we spot a critical issue during the pilot—like a compliance problem or something that's causing patient delays—what's the escalation path? Do we pause and fix, or do we document and keep going?

Good question. If it's a critical issue—compliance, patient safety, or significant delays—we pause and fix immediately. If it's a minor issue or a process tweak, we document it and keep going. I'll be available for quick calls if you need to escalate. Let's define 'critical' as anything that could impact patient care or compliance. Everything else we log in A6 and address in the post-pilot review.

That makes sense. I'm assuming we're also collecting baseline metrics before the pilot starts, right? Error rates, average intake time, that kind of thing? We'll need that to compare against the pilot metrics.

Exactly. I'll pull baseline data from the past month—error rates, intake times, rework incidents, anything we can measure. That goes into A6 as the baseline. Then during the pilot, we track the same metrics daily and compare at the end. That's part of T8.
Good. And we're also collecting staff feedback during the pilot, right? Not just metrics, but what staff think is working and what's not?

Yes. 529990 will collect feedback during the daily check-ins and we'll do a quick survey at the end of week one and again at the end of the pilot. That feedback goes into A6 and will inform the post-pilot adjustments. Alright, let me confirm D7: pilot runs Monday 15th through Friday 26th in Unit A, with daily check-ins and weekly team syncs. 529990 is the primary contact. Does everyone agree?
Confirmed. I'm ready to go. I'll send the first check-in on Monday at 4 PM. One last thing: should I be documenting everything in A6, or is there a separate log I should be using?

Everything goes into A6. It's a shared tracker with columns for date, issue, resolution, metrics, and feedback. I'll set it up this week and share access with you. You'll update it daily with your check-in notes. That way, everything is in one place and easy to review.

Sounds good. I'll be monitoring from my end too and can jump in if you need support, 529990. Let's make sure we're all aligned on the daily check-in format. Should it be a quick message in this thread, or a separate update?

Good question. Let's do the daily check-ins as a separate thread in this channel—'Pilot Daily Check-in'—so they don't clutter the main thread. That way, we can keep the main thread for bigger updates and decisions. 529990, you'll post there each day at 4 PM. Sound good?
Perfect. I'll start the daily check-in thread on Monday. Alright, I think we're ready. Pilot starts Monday 15th. Let's make this work.

threads.thread_goal: Review pilot results and agree on adjustments and rollout plan

messages.text: Pilot is complete. Great work to everyone, especially 529990 for the daily coordination. I've compiled the pilot evaluation report in A7. Here's the summary: error rates dropped by 18%, intake time increased slightly (about 3 minutes per patient on average), but staff feedback was very positive. The main issues we found were: (1) the capacity assessment decision tree needed a small clarification, (2) one form field was confusing to patients, and (3) staff wanted a quick reference card for the new consent process. I've drafted updates to A2 and A3 based on these findings, and I've also prepared the full rollout implementation plan in T10. Please review A7 and the updated documents, and let me know if you agree with the proposed changes and the rollout approach.

Great results. The 18% drop in errors is significant. I agree with the proposed changes—the capacity assessment clarification makes sense, and the form field fix is straightforward. One thing I want to flag: during the pilot, we noticed that staff were asking a lot of questions about what to do if a patient doesn't have ID. Should we add guidance on that to A2?
Good catch. I'll add a section to A2 on alternative identification procedures. That's a real scenario and staff need clear guidance. I'll include it in the final version.

I've reviewed the rollout plan in T10 and it looks solid. Three phases over three months, with clear ownership and dates. One question: are we planning to do any training refresher for the units that weren't in the pilot, or do we assume the materials we created are sufficient?

Good question. I think we should do at least one live training session for each new unit, plus the async materials. The pilot taught us that live training is really valuable for answering questions and building confidence. I'll include that in the rollout plan. We can also use staff from Unit A as co-trainers for the new units—they've been through it and can share their experience.

That's a good approach. Using pilot staff as co-trainers builds buy-in and spreads the knowledge. I've also reviewed the updated A2 and A3, and I'm satisfied with the changes. The capacity assessment clarification is good, and the form field fix addresses the issue we saw. I'm ready to approve these for rollout.
I agree. The updated documents are solid. One more thing: should we also update A4 (the quick-reference checklist) to include the new guidance on alternative ID and the consent quick reference card?

Absolutely. I'll update A4 to include the alternative ID guidance and add the consent quick reference card. That's part of T9. I'll also create a change log documenting all the adjustments we made based on pilot feedback.

Good. So to summarise: we're updating A2, A3, and A4 based on pilot feedback, we're including live training for each new unit in the rollout, and we're using pilot staff as co-trainers. The rollout plan in T10 covers three phases over three months. Is that right?

Exactly. And we're also preparing A8 (the post-rollout monitoring guide) and T12 (the monitoring routine). Those will define how we track the new workflow after rollout and escalate issues. I'll have all of that ready by end of week. Once we confirm D8, we're ready to move forward with full rollout.
I'm ready to confirm D8. The updated SOP and forms are solid, the rollout plan is clear, and the monitoring approach is defined. I think we're ready to move forward.
Agreed. I'm confident in the plan. One last thing: should we also prepare a communication pack for staff about the rollout? Something that explains what's changing and why?

Great point. That's T11. I'll prepare a communication pack with an announcement message, FAQ, and talking points for managers. That'll help staff understand the changes and feel supported. I'll have that ready by end of week too.

Perfect. So we have: updated A2, A3, A4; rollout plan in T10; monitoring guide in A8; communication pack in T11; and monitoring routine in T12. That covers everything. I think we're ready to confirm D8 and move forward with rollout.

Confirmed. D8 is locked in. We're approving the final adjusted SOP and forms (A2, A3), the full rollout implementation plan (T10), the monitoring guide (A8), and the monitoring routine (T12). Rollout begins next week with Phase 1. I'll send out the communication pack and training schedule by Friday. Great work, everyone. This has been a solid project.
